subject: GPU pool SLA classes, warmup & headroom recommendations for Lighthouse Analytics
messages:
From: Ben Jensen <ben.jensen@lighthouse.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: partner-success@lighthouse.io
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private pool sizing: projected sustained QPS and warmup requirements

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Lighthouse is getting into final procurement for a private VPC deployment and we need concrete capacity guidance so our infra team can size the rack layout and networking. A few facts and asks up front: 

- Model: LlamaX-70B (4-bit quantized variant) for generation and chat.
- Expected steady workload: 1,200 QPS (text-generation calls) during business-critical windows (roughly 08:00–20:00 PT).
- Short peaks: up to 2,500 QPS for ~20-minute bursts (marketing pushes).
- Typical sequence length: 512 tokens; average response ~100 tokens.
- Hard SLA target for conversation flows: p95 latency <= 300ms end-to-end (we consider 150–200ms ideal for premium customers).

Questions for Redwood:
1) How would you recommend we classify SLA tiers for this private pool (Gold/Silver/Bronze) and map them to throughput/latency targets?
2) What headroom margin do you recommend (percentage of capacity reserved for burst absorption)?
3) Warmup strategy: how many GPUs/nodes should we prewarm and what KV cache prefill strategy do you support for private deployments?
4) Any specific networking (MTU, NIC offload, egress limits) or rack-level guidance we should add to our procurement spec?

We'd like a short write-up from your side we can attach to the RFP. If useful we can set a 45-minute workshop with your infra team.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Private pool sizing: projected sustained QPS and warmup requirements

Ben / team,

Following up with a draft sizing and operational guidance. This is a pragmatic starting point — we'll refine in the workshop after we look at your p95 logs and topology. High level recommendations: 

1) SLA classes (three service classes with clear throughput/latency bands)
   - Gold: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 150ms. Target for premium customers. Invest in smaller batch sizes, aggressive KV caching, reserved GPU pool (no preemption).
   - Silver: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms. Standard production traffic; autoscale with short cool-down.
   - Bronze: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 500ms. Best-effort; long-tail jobs and large generation requests.

2) Capacity math (ballpark for LlamaX-70B 4-bit variant)
   - Baseline throughput per A100-80GB-equivalent instance (quantized runtime, with our optimized kernels): ~45–60 QPS for 512/100 token workload at p95 ~200ms when using 1-2 microbatches.
   - For your steady 1,200 QPS: ~22–27 GPUs baseline.
   - For 2,500 QPS burst with 40% headroom target: plan for 2,500 / 45 ≈ 56 GPUs logical capacity; with node packing and buffer, recommend reserved pool = 60 GPUs, or equivalent fractional nodes depending on chosen instance size.
   - Recommended headroom: 30–40% for marketing bursts and cache churn. We prefer pre-allocated burst nodes (ReservedCapacity) rather than elastically spinning entirely cold nodes for high-concurrency bursts.

3) Warmup & KV cache strategy
   - Prewarm approach: keep a small ring of warm GPUs (~10–15% of steady baseline) that hold KV caches for most common prompt prefixes (top-200 prefixes). On forecasted bursts, scale up warm instances in 2–3 minutes while routing lower-priority traffic to Bronze class.
   - KV prefill: Redwood's private runtime can accept pre-seeded cache snapshots. We recommend a scheduled nightly snapshot and delta sync morning-of heavy windows.

4) Networking & rack guidance
   - NIC: 100Gbps top-of-rack recommended; enable LRO/GRO and RSS to spread traffic. MTU=9000 where possible to reduce CPU overhead for large payloads.
   - Egress: ensure capacity for peak token egress; estimate ~token-size*QPS*avg_token_length — for your numbers plan for ~20–30 Gbps egress headroom.
   - Keep instance placement aware of intra-pod affinity to reduce cross-rack latency for KV fetches.

5) Autoscaling policy suggestions
   - Scale-up trigger: p95 latency crossing target for 3 consecutive 30s windows OR queue length > threshold.
   - Scale-down: grace period 5–10 minutes to avoid oscillation.

6) Canary & fallback
   - Use canary rollout on 10% traffic for new model variants; shard by customer to avoid broad impact. Maintain automatic fallback to smaller model or hosted Redwood endpoint if private capacity is exhausted.

I've attached a quick CSV with sizing permutations (sizing-estimates.csv). We'll bring refined numbers to the workshop.

--Priyom
